48167-the-children-of-the-valley.title: The Children Of The Valley
48167-the-children-of-the-valley.creator: Harriet
48167-the-children-of-the-valley.description: A book by Harriet. “Of course,” said Old Uncle, “they’ll bring her back! Ally’ll turn up all right—she makes more noise, when she sets about it, than all the rest of you put together!” Nevertheless, Old Uncle—who believed in whipping, at least he said he did—was making for the hollows of Blue Top as he said it. For Ally was really the darling of the household, always bright and sweet-tempered, and daring and ready for anything.

arxiv-2105-10131.title: Visual representation of negation: Real world data analysis on comic image design
arxiv-2105-10131.creator: Yuri Sato, Koji Mineshima, and Kazuhiro Ueda
arxiv-2105-10131.description: Abstract There has been a widely held view that visual representations (e.g., photographs and illustrations) do not depict negation, for example, one that can be expressed by a sentence “the train is not coming”. This view is empirically challenged by analyzing the real-world visual representations of comic (manga) illustrations.

arxiv-2105-11147.title: Harmless but Useful: Beyond Separable Equality Constraints in Datalog+/- Conference: ; ;
arxiv-2105-11147.creator: Luigi Bellomarini, Emanuel Sallinger
arxiv-2105-11147.description: Abstract . Ontological query answering is the problem of answering queries in the presence of schema constraints representing the domain of interest. Datalog+/- is a commonly adopted family of languages for schema constraints, which includes tuple-generating dependencies (TGDs) and equality-generating dependencies (EGDs).

arxiv-2107-03542.title: Learning quantum phases via single-qubit disentanglement
arxiv-2107-03542.creator: Zheng An, Chenfeng Cao, Cheng-Qian Xu, D. L. Zhou
arxiv-2107-03542.description: Abstract Identifying phases of matter presents considerable challenges, particularly within the domain of quantum theory, where the complexity of ground states appears to increase exponentially with system size. Quantum many-body systems exhibit an array of complex entanglement structures spanning distinct phases.

arxiv-2209-00065.title: ViA: View-invariant Skeleton Action Representation Learning via Motion Retargeting
arxiv-2209-00065.creator: Di Yang Yaohui Wang Antitza Dantcheva Lorenzo Garattoni, Gianpiero Francesca François Brémond
arxiv-2209-00065.description: Abstract Current self-supervised approaches for skeleton action representation learning often focus on constrained scenarios, where videos and skeleton data are recorded in laboratory settings. When dealing with estimated skeleton data in real-world videos , such methods perform poorly due to the large variations across subjects and camera viewpoints.

arxiv-2211-12094.title: Fast Multiplex Graph Association Rules for Link Prediction
arxiv-2211-12094.creator: Michele Coscia, Christian Borgelt
arxiv-2211-12094.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Michele Coscia, Christian Borgelt. Multiplex networks allow us to study a variety of complex systems where nodes connect to each other in multiple ways, for example friend, family, and co-worker relations in social networks. Link prediction is the branch of network analysis allowing us to forecast the future status of a network: which new connections are the most likely to appear in the future? In multiplex link prediction we also ask: of which type?

arxiv-2212-13476.title: On bisectors in quaternionic hyperbolic space Thanks: Corresponding author.
arxiv-2212-13476.creator: Igor A.R. Almeida
arxiv-2212-13476.description: Abstract In this paper, we study a problem related to geometry of bisectors in quaternionic hyperbolic geometry. We develop some of the basic theory of bisectors in quaternionic hyperbolic space H ℚ n {\rm H^{n}_{\mathbb{Q}}} . In particular, we show that quaternionic bisectors enjoy various decompositions by totally geodesic submanifolds of H ℚ n {\rm H^{n}_{\mathbb{Q}}} .

arxiv-2407-06034.title: About Wess-Zumino-Witten equation and Harder-Narasimhan potentials
arxiv-2407-06034.creator: Siarhei Finski
arxiv-2407-06034.description: Abstract MnLargeSymbols’164 MnLargeSymbols’171 Abstract. For a polarized family of complex projective manifolds, we identify the algebraic obstructions that govern the existence of approximate solutions to the Wess-Zumino-Witten equation. When this is specialized to the fibration associated with a projectivization of a vector bundle, we recover a version of Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence.

arxiv-2504-18567.title: Joint Simulation Study of Chiral Symmetry Recovery and Transport Response in QCD at Finite Temperature and Chemical Potentials
arxiv-2504-18567.creator: Jingxu Wu, Yuwei Yin, Jianing Shi
arxiv-2504-18567.description: Abstract We investigate QCD matter using the two-flavor PNJL model and find that the shear viscosity to entropy density ratio η / s \eta/s reaches a minimum while the bulk viscosity ζ / s \zeta/s peaks near the chiral crossover line, particularly at large baryon chemical potential, indicating sensitivity to critical dynamics and offering potential signatures for the QCD critical

arxiv-2507-05041.title: Magnetic flux threading a planar holed superconductor Preprint: v004 - August 8, 2026
arxiv-2507-05041.creator: Jaume Cunill-Subiranas, Natanael Bort-Soldevila, Nuria Del-Valle, Carles Navau
arxiv-2507-05041.description: Abstract We analytically evaluate the currents in a planar-holed ideal (perfect magnetic shielding) superconductor when an axial dipole is located along the system’s axis, obtaining a simple relation between the fluxoid (in this geometry, it equals the flux) threading the hole, the net current circling it, and the magnitude and position of the dipole.

arxiv-2512-16014.title: Magneto-optical Kerr effect in pump-probe setups
arxiv-2512-16014.creator: Amir Eskandari-asl, Adolfo Avella
arxiv-2512-16014.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amir Eskandari-asl, Adolfo Avella. We develop a general theoretical framework for computing the time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect in ultrafast pump–probe setups, formulated within the Dynamical Projective Operatorial Approach (DPOA) and its application to the generalized linear-response theory for pumped systems. Furthermore, we exploit this formalism to express the post-pump optical conductivity — and consequently the Kerr rotation — in terms of the time-evolved single-particle density matrix (SPDM), providing a transparent and computationally efficient description of photo-excited multi-band systems.

pmc-10559430.title: Hemostatic effect and safety evaluation of oxidized regenerated cellulose in total knee arthroplasty- a randomized controlledtrial
pmc-10559430.creator: Bowei Li, Wenjie Pan, Xiaobo Sun, Kai Qin, Guoyang Bai, Huanli Bao, Yuanchi Huang, Jianbing Ma
pmc-10559430.description: BackgroundOxidized regenerated cellulose (ORC) is a type of biodegradable hemostatic material, which has been widely used in the field of surgery. However, its hemostatic effect in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is uncertain. Accordingly, this study investigated the effectiveness and safety of ORC in patients receiving TKA.

pmc-11506440.title: Otolaryngology Diagnoses at a Student-Run Community Clinic
pmc-11506440.creator: Brian P Quinlan, Wilhelmina Tan, Orly Coblens, Brian McKinnon
pmc-11506440.description: PurposeCompared to insured individuals who have established pathways for primary and specialist care, uninsured patients often delay seeking medical attention and are more likely to rely on emergency departments or community clinics for low-cost services. This study aims to identify the most prevalent otolaryngology (ENT) diagnoses at a free, student-run community clinic for uninsured patients.

pmc-11543159.description: represents the syndrome’s four classic features: susceptibility to warts induced by human papillomavirus infection, hypogammaglobulinemia, infections, and myelokathexsis1​. The exact prevalence of WHIM syndrome is unknown, but it is estimated to occur in approximately one in every five million live births.

pmc-12366083.title: Combining mindfulness intervention and open-label placebo treatment for chronic pain: a protocol for a feasibility study
pmc-12366083.creator: Chung Jung Mun, Estrella Contreras, Yushu Xiao, Ryan Eckert, Alexandra Harting, Sathvika Damera, Iosef Perez, Hemant K. Pandey, Aram S. Mardian, Frank LoVecchio, Luana Colloca, Kelly E. Dunn, Michael Todd, Roger B. Fillingim, Mary C. Davis
pmc-12366083.description: BackgroundMindfulness-based interventions, such as mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR), are efficacious mind–body treatments for chronic pain, though their modest effect sizes suggest room for improvement. Notably, recent studies indicate that mindfulness meditation does not engage the endogenous opioid system, which plays an important role in analgesia.

pmc-12445782.title: Understanding the Thoughts and Preferences for Technologies Designed to Detect Feelings of Loneliness: Interview Study Among Older Adults
pmc-12445782.creator: Jessica Rees, John Ratcliffe, Wei Liu, Yi Zhou, Sebastien Ourselin, Michela Antonelli, Ashay Patel, Yu Shi, Jingqi Liu, Anthea Tinker, Faith Matcham
pmc-12445782.description: BackgroundLoneliness is a negative emotional state that is common in later life. The accumulative effects of loneliness have a significant impact on the physical and mental health of older adults. Automatic methods for detection and prediction are an emerging field to support early identification of loneliness.

pmc-12470074.title: Parental Self-Efficacy in Managing Pediatrics’ Medications and Treatments in Jordan: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12470074.creator: Abdallah Y Naser, Hassan Al-Shehri, Alasdair Barr
pmc-12470074.description: Background: Parents make vital decisions regarding their children’s health and safety. Poor parental self-efficacy is associated with unfavorable health outcomes among their children. This study aims to investigate parental self-efficacy in managing pediatric medications and treatments in Jordan. Methods: This is an online cross-sectional survey study that was conducted in Jordan between 20 April and 4 July 2025.

pmc-12561783.title: Optimizing Biodegradable Poly(D,L-lactide) Scaffolds Reinforced with Graphene Oxide for Bone Tissue Regeneration
pmc-12561783.creator: Esperanza Díaz, Ander García, Xabier León, Yolanda Merodio, Sylvie Ribeiro, Senentxu Lanceros-Méndez, Tun Naw Sut, Bo Kyeong Yoon
pmc-12561783.description: This study investigates the potential of porous poly(D,L-lactide) (PDLLA) scaffolds reinforced with graphene oxide (GO) for bone tissue engineering applications. Scaffolds were fabricated using thermally induced phase separation (TIPS) and characterized in terms of morphology, biodegradation, thermal and mechanical properties, and cytocompatibility.

pmc-12654067.title: Study of Heat Transfer Characteristics of PCMs Melting Inside Aluminum Foams
pmc-12654067.creator: Farjad Shahid Hasan Khan, Andrea Diani, Antonio Caggiano
pmc-12654067.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study examines the thermal performance of phase change material (PCM)–metal foam composites under base heating, a configuration more relevant to compact thermal energy storage (TES) and electronics-cooling applications, compared to the widely studied side-heated case. Metal foams with pore densities of 10, 20, and 40 PPI, but identical porosity (volumetric value), were impregnated with two PCMs (paraffin RT55 and RT64HC) and tested under varying heat fluxes.

pmc-13546239.title: Social Workers’ Perspectives on the Climate of Trauma-Informed and Non-Trauma-Informed Schools
pmc-13546239.creator: Kate R. Watson, Ron Avi Astor, Gordon P. Capp, Rami Benbenishty
pmc-13546239.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study explored school climate from the perspective of social workers, documenting their perceptions of trauma-informed culture and climate in U.S. Using logistic regression, we analyzed survey data from 538 school social workers to investigate whether their experiences of school climate characteristics associated with trauma-informed approaches—physical and psychological safety; a focus on strengths and equity; and supportive relationships—were associated with their identification of a school as trauma informed.
